text.p: Investors should hold their shares in Polish trader Universal SA, which looks slightly undervalued despite certain balance sheet problems, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA said in a report dated December 11, 1996.

"The current market price (eight zlotys) of Universal SA is about eight to 15 percent lower than the estimated value of the company's shares, which provides the investor with a certain safety margin. This is why we recommend holding shares of Universal SA," the report said.
The stock closed at 8.2 zlotys on Monday.

Handlowy said Universal was successfully building a capital group with overlapping specialisation in several selected areas of trade and was finding new domestic and foreign markets, including in the former Soviet Union.
"The vertical integration of entities in the group will significantly faciliate the realisation of the company's plans," the report said.

But it said Universal suffered from an ever lengthening accounts receivable repayment period, a high 25-percent doubtful accounts receivable percentage and short-term liablilites used to finance long-term activities.
It also said Universal had high costs of outside financing, a relatively high level of non-balance sheet liabilities and a low effectiveness of operating activity.

Handlowy said that its predicted 1996 net profit for Universal of 23 million zlotys would likely fall to 14.6 million zlotys in 1997. Sales would rise to 132 million from 118 million zlotys. The firm received tax and interest refunds of 16 million zlotys last year.
The stock would trade at eight times estimated 1996 earnings and 12.7 times estimated 1997 earnings.
Its price to book ratio would fall to 0.8 from 0.84.
